briefings.title: BREAKING: JD Vance Speaks With Press After Iran Says US Violated Ceasefire—Closes Strait Of Hormuz

people.name: JD Vance
people.role: Vice President of the United States

briefings.tldr: Vice President JD Vance confirmed a tenuous ceasefire is in effect with Iran, clarifying that upcoming negotiations in Islamabad will prioritize the permanent reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and the removal of nuclear fuel, while explicitly stating that Lebanon was never included in the current truce.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Vice President JD Vance confirmed a tenuous ceasefire is in effect with Iran, clarifying that upcoming negotiations in Islamabad will prioritize the permanent reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and the removal of nuclear fuel, while explicitly stating that Lebanon was never included in the current truce.

## Diplomatic Mission to Hungary
* **Counteracting EU Influence:** Vance stated the primary purpose of his trip was to counteract "propaganda" from the European Union bureaucracy in Brussels.
    * **Election Interference:** He accused the EU of attempting to impose costs on the Hungarian people to sway election results, calling the practice "absurd."
* **Support for Viktor Orbán:** Vance reaffirmed that both he and President Trump give their "full support" to Prime Minister Orbán and the Hungarian people.

## Clarifying the Iran Ceasefire Framework
* **The "Three Proposals" Problem:** Vance warned the public against "maximalist" or fake proposals circulating in the media. 
    * **Rejected Drafts:** One ten-point proposal was reportedly written by AI (ChatGPT) and immediately rejected by U.S. negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner.
    * **Legitimate Framework:** The official proposal, referenced by President Trump, was developed through back-and-forth negotiations involving U.S., Iranian, and Pakistani officials.
* **Strait of Hormuz Status:** Vance reported that while the waterway is starting to reopen and oil prices are stabilizing, the U.S. will only abide by ceasefire terms if the Straits remain open for traffic.
* **Media Criticism:** Vance criticized major outlets like the *New York Times* and *CNN* for reporting "fringe" Iranian leaks as official negotiating positions.

## Regional Conflicts and Lebanon
* **Lebanon Exclusion:** Vance clarified a "legitimate misunderstanding" regarding the scope of the ceasefire. He stated the U.S. never promised to include Lebanon in the truce; the agreement is focused strictly on Iran and U.S. allies (Israel and Gulf Arab states).
* **Israeli Posture:** While not a condition of the ceasefire, Vance noted that Israel has offered to "check themselves" regarding strikes in Lebanon to facilitate the success of the broader negotiation.
* **Negotiation Team:** Vance credited Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner as the primary "on the ground" negotiators, supported by a broader team including Pete Hegseth and Marco Rubio.

## Nuclear Objectives and Leverage
* **Primary Demands:** The U.S. objective remains preventing Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon. Specifically, the U.S. is demanding that Iran "give up the nuclear fuel."
* **Negotiating Carrots and Sticks:**
    * **Economic Incentives:** Sanctions relief and economic partnerships are on the table, but only if Iran makes firm commitments to end nuclear development.
    * **Military Leverage:** Vance defended the President’s aggressive rhetoric, stating that if Iran breaks the bargain, they will face "serious consequences" from the U.S. military.
* **Response to Mohammad Ghalibaf:** Addressing the Iranian Parliament Speaker’s complaints that three points of the plan were violated, Vance argued that if only three points are in dispute, it suggests there is broad agreement on the remaining points of the 15-point framework.

> "The first ten-point proposal was something that was submitted, and we think frankly was probably written by ChatGPT... That immediately went in the garbage and was rejected." — JD Vance

> "I actually think this comes from a legitimate misunderstanding. I think the Iranians thought that the ceasefire included Lebanon and it just didn't. We never made that promise." — JD Vance

> "My wife has the right to skydive. But she doesn't jump out of an airplane because she and I have an agreement that she's not going to do that... We don't really concern ourselves with what they claim they have the right to do, we concern ourselves with what they actually do." — JD Vance (on Iran's "right" to enrich uranium)

briefings.title: BREAKING NEWS: JD Vance Holds Event In Hungary After U.S. And Iran Agree To 2-Week Ceasefire

people.name: JD Vance
people.role: Vice President of the United States

briefings.tldr: Vice President JD Vance’s visit to Budapest underscores a burgeoning "conservative international" alliance, where he defended Hungarian sovereignty against EU pressure and announced a "fragile" 12-hour-old ceasefire agreement with Iran.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Vice President JD Vance’s visit to Budapest underscores a burgeoning "conservative international" alliance, where he defended Hungarian sovereignty against EU pressure and announced a "fragile" 12-hour-old ceasefire agreement with Iran.

## Breakthrough in the Middle East: Iran Ceasefire
* **Ceasefire Terms:** VP Vance announced a tentative truce reached with Tehran approximately 8-12 hours prior to his speech.
    * **Strategic Concessions:** Iran has agreed to open the Straits of Hormuz and cease threats to the global economy. In exchange, the U.S. and its allies have agreed to halt active attacks.
    * **Military Objectives:** Vance asserted that the U.S. successfully achieved its goal of decimating Iran’s conventional military capabilities before entering negotiations.
* **Diplomatic Skepticism:** Vance characterized the truce as "fragile," noting internal divisions within the Iranian government.
    * While the Iranian Foreign Minister signals a willingness to negotiate, Vance accused other factions within the Iranian system of lying about the nature of the military damage and the agreement terms.
    * **Economic Leverage:** The VP warned that if Iran "cheats," the U.S. maintains "extraordinary economic leverage" and an "impatient" President ready to resume pressure.

## National Sovereignty and Foreign Influence
* **Defining Influence:** Vance pushed back against critics who labeled his visit as "foreign influence," arguing that true interference comes from transnational organizations.
    * **Criticism of Brussels:** He condemned the European Union for withholding billions in funding to pressure Hungary on border policy and education reform.
    * **Ukrainian Pressure:** Vance described Ukrainian threats to shut down pipelines or target Hungarian officials as "scandalous" and an "assault on sovereignty."
* **Support for Viktor Orbán:** Vance praised Prime Minister Orbán as a "partner for peace," specifically noting Orbán’s ability to understand both Russian and Ukrainian positions—a prerequisite he deems necessary for a peaceful settlement.
* **The Symbolism of Sovereignty:** Vance referenced the Crown of Saint Stephen in the Hungarian Parliament as a reminder that power belongs to the Hungarian people, not "Brussels bureaucrats."

## Reforming the University Model
* **Institutional Mission:** Balázs Orbán (Chairman, MCC) framed the Mathias Corvinus Collegium as a "mission" to educate patriotic Hungarians capable of international competition while remaining rooted in national values.
* **Vance on Educational Ideology:** The VP praised Hungary for imposing "democratic constraints" on education funding.
    * **Defunding Ideology:** He argued that taxpayers should not be forced to fund "radical gender ideology" or "civil unrest" in academic settings.
    * **US Policy Shifts:** Vance highlighted recent U.S. efforts to end race-based discrimination in admissions and promote a "meritocracy" that draws students from diverse geographic backgrounds rather than just "insular" elite social networks.
* **The Role of the Academy:** Vance argued that universities should serve two primary functions: providing "useful skills" for the workforce and fostering the ability to "think critically" to participate in democracy.

## Geopolitics and Elite Social Networks
* **Energy Policy Critiques:** Vance criticized European leadership for creating an energy crisis by becoming dependent on Russia while simultaneously labeling Russia a security threat. He contrasted this with U.S. policy aimed at "energy dominance."
* **The "Insular" Elite:** Reflecting on his time at Yale Law School, Vance noted that political centers like D.C. and Brussels have become self-reinforcing networks that are disconnected from "normal" citizens.
* **Advice to Students:** He urged young conservatives to avoid "blackpilling" (cynical withdrawal from politics).
    * **Persistence:** He emphasized that "civilization was not built overnight" and requires long-term institutional building rather than instant gratification.

## Notable Quotes

> "Foreign influence is when other governments threaten, cajole, and try to use economic influence to tell you how to vote... That is fundamentally an assault on your sovereignty." — **JD Vance**

> "The Iranians are better negotiators than they are fighters... if they negotiate in good faith, we will be able to find a deal, but that’s a big 'if'." — **JD Vance**

> "Taxpayer funding is not unlimited... You can say whatever you want, but in Hungary, you don’t get unlimited subsidy if you want to say something that’s really crazy or that promotes violence." — **JD Vance**

> "Blackpilling is how you give power to the forces that are trying to destroy what our ancestors built. We need to take power back from those people and build the kind of institutions that can actually save our society." — **JD Vance**

briefings.title: Beyond the IT Headlines | Inside the AI Data Factory: How Enterprise AI Gets Built
briefings.tldr: The enterprise AI landscape has shifted from experimental training to "always-on" production (inference), requiring a fundamental transition toward "AI Data Factories"—architectural blueprints rather than single products—where data is continuously processed by autonomous agents to drive core business outcomes.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
The enterprise AI landscape has shifted from experimental training to "always-on" production (inference), requiring a fundamental transition toward "AI Data Factories"—architectural blueprints rather than single products—where data is continuously processed by autonomous agents to drive core business outcomes.

## From AI Training to "Inference-First" Operations
* **Defining the Inflection Point:** Jensen Huang’s keynote at NVIDIA GTC declared that the era of inference has arrived. Kaycee Lai clarifies that "inference" simply means actually *using* AI in production to solve business problems rather than just prepping models.
* **Operationalizing AI:** While personal and entertainment AI have flourished, enterprises have been slow to operationalize. The "AI Data Factory" represents a shift where AI is no longer a single app or SaaS tool but is core to every department and data stream.
* **The "Always-On" Demand:** Unlike training, which is a means to an end, inference in a factory setting runs 24/7. Modern data estates must evolve to handle a massive increase in velocity, moving from answering one question every three months to potentially thirty questions per second.

## The Architecture of the AI Data Factory
* **The Factory Analogy:** Kaycee Lai breaks down the components of an AI factory to move past marketing jargon:
    * **Inputs:** Raw data from across the enterprise.
    * **The "Plumbing":** Physical infrastructure including servers, networking, storage, compute, power, and space.
    * **The Process:** Models and applications that transform data.
    * **The Output:** Consumable value such as applications, data sets, or automated documentation.
* **Not a Single SKU:** Despite many vendors selling "AI Factories," it is not a single product. Like a bread factory versus a car factory, every AI factory will look different based on the specific business problem it is designed to solve.
* **NVIDIA’s Blueprint:** NVIDIA is positioning itself as a provider of "reference architectures"—essentially the road systems, traffic lights, and lane markers—upon which enterprises must build their own specific "vehicles."

## The Rise of Autonomous Workers (CLAW)
* **Defining CLAW:** An emerging concept in the industry is the **Continuous Learning Autonomous Worker (CLAW)**—agents that are always learning, autonomous, and capable of mimicking human-level task coordination.
* **From Single Agents to Orchestration:** The industry is moving from single-threaded agents to multi-agent frameworks. 
    * **Nemo CLAW:** NVIDIA’s framework designed to provide the governance, security, and "sniff test" required by IT departments to trust autonomous agents with corporate data and policies.
* **Agentic Workflows:** Kaycee Lai describes building internal tools (e.g., "Abbie") where multiple agents coordinate to research a client, identify AI use cases, and generate tailored sales collateral in seconds based on a single prompt.
* **The Resource Impact:** Agents do not sleep or take vacations. An autonomous worker continuously generating output also continuously consumes storage, networking, and GPU resources, requiring a highly resilient infrastructure.

## Strategic Roadmap: Working Backward for the CIO
* **The Infrastructure Trap:** Many CIOs are buying high-performance GPUs and infrastructure before identifying their specific use cases. Lai warns that the world’s most powerful "power drill" is wasted if the user doesn't know what they are building.
* **The "Hostess" Methodology:** To avoid AI failure, enterprises should work backward through the supply chain:
    1. **Identify the "Snack":** What does the customer want to buy? (The Business Outcome).
    2. **Source the Ingredients:** What data is required to produce that outcome? (Data Readiness).
    3. **Build the Factory:** What specific infrastructure and toolsets are needed to process that data at scale?
* **Core Business Use Cases:** AI success is often found in traditional problems made faster, such as predictive maintenance in manufacturing or real-time inventory planning in supply chain management.

## Notable Quotes

> "Inference means you're actually using it. It's as simple as that... The technology is ready for people to actually consume inference safely and on a regular basis in production." — **Kaycee Lai**

> "It doesn't matter how great the performance is, if you actually don't even know what the use case you're trying to solve for... you're never going to actually use the infrastructure in a way that's going to deliver value." — **Kaycee Lai**

> "NVIDIA is providing the road system, the traffic lights, the stop signs, the lane markers, the speed limits, and then essentially asking enterprises to go put their cars on the road to go where they need to." — **Shawn Rosemarin**

> "An efficient factory is constantly running, consuming inputs and generating outputs... Every single time I have wait time where trucks aren't getting loaded, I'm losing money." — **Kaycee Lai**

briefings.title: Insights from a 25-Year Monetary Policy Experiment | Paul Sheard
briefings.tldr: Paul Sheard traces the 25-year evolution of Quantitative Easing (QE) from a 2001 Japanese experiment to a global monetary standard, highlighting how the technical ability to pay interest on bank reserves fundamentally changed how central banks manage liquidity and interest rates.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Paul Sheard traces the 25-year evolution of Quantitative Easing (QE) from a 2001 Japanese experiment to a global monetary standard, highlighting how the technical ability to pay interest on bank reserves fundamentally changed how central banks manage liquidity and interest rates.

## Origins and Global Adoption of Quantitative Easing
*   **The Japanese Experiment:** The modern era of QE began on March 19, 2001, at the Bank of Japan. Initially viewed as a "Japanese curiosity," it remained a local phenomenon for seven years before the 2008 financial crisis forced its adoption globally.
*   **US Implementation:** In response to the 2008 collapse, the Federal Reserve pivoted from emergency "credit easing" to purposeful QE, buying Treasuries and mortgage-backed securities to inject liquidity.
*   **Balance Sheet Growth:** The Fed’s balance sheet ratcheted up from pre-2008 levels to a peak of approximately $9 trillion by late 2023. It has since entered a "quantitative tightening" phase, currently sitting at roughly $6.5 trillion.

## Mechanics of the Central Bank Balance Sheet
*   **Asset Composition:** Central bank assets primarily consist of government bonds and debt securities. These are paid for through the creation of "reserves"—base money created "out of thin air."
*   **Key Liabilities:** The Fed’s balance sheet is balanced by three primary liability components:
    *   **Reserves:** Deposits that commercial banks hold at the central bank.
    *   **Banknotes:** Physical currency in circulation (Federal Reserve Notes). Notably, these are signed by the US Treasurer, not the Fed Chair.
    *   **Government Deposits:** The Treasury’s own bank account held at the Fed, which fluctuates based on tax revenue and government spending (e.g., Social Security or military payments).
*   **The Accounting Identity:** The level of reserves in the banking system is mathematically determined by the other components. If the public withdraws cash or the government collects taxes, reserves go down unless the central bank offsets this by purchasing more assets.

## The "Interest on Reserves" (IOR) Turning Point
*   **Legislative Shift:** Under the 2008 TARP legislation, the Federal Reserve was granted the legal authority to pay interest on reserves. This power was originally slated for 2011 but was accelerated to manage the crisis.
*   **Decoupling Policy:** Before 2008, the Fed could not pay interest on excess reserves. If banks had too much liquidity, they would try to "dump" it, naturally forcing the interest rate to zero. 
*   **The "Floor" System:** By paying interest on reserves, the Fed gained the ability to raise the federal funds rate even with a "bloated" balance sheet. This allowed them to tighten monetary policy without having to sell off all the assets they acquired during QE.

## Operational Dynamics of Monetary Policy
*   **The Federal Funds Rate:** This is the interest rate at which commercial banks trade reserves among themselves overnight on the Fed’s balance sheet.
*   **Open Market Operations:** The Fed acts as the "last mover" in the money market. Because they can track fiscal flows and banknote demand daily, they use the purchase or sale of assets to precisely hit their reserve and interest rate targets.
*   **Transition from Reactive to Proactive:** Historically, the Fed reactively adjusted reserves to match minimum requirements. In the post-QE era, they proactively manage the massive "cloud" of excess reserves through interest rate floors.

***

> "Initially for the first seven years or so, what the Bank of Japan was doing—so-called QE—was this kind of Japanese curiosity... not realizing that before too long, it was coming to [global] shores as well." — Paul Sheard

> "The central bank has the privilege of being able to create money out of thin air. Commercial banks can, as well, but that’s a different story." — Paul Sheard

> "It was a corollary of the fact that you had a positive interest rate... and no interest on reserves, that the Fed had no choice but to passively, reactively adjust the level of reserves." — Paul Sheard

briefings.title: Josh Shapiro on Trump, Iran War Chaos, Israel's Failure, the Economy, and 2028 Race
briefings.tldr: Governor Josh Shapiro details his "Pennsylvania Model" of governance—prioritizing operational efficiency ("Getting Shit Done"), pro-growth economic policies, and aggressive fraud prosecution—as a centrist blueprint for the Democratic Party to counter federal "chaos and corruption."
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR:** Governor Josh Shapiro details his "Pennsylvania Model" of governance—prioritizing operational efficiency ("Getting Shit Done"), pro-growth economic policies, and aggressive fraud prosecution—as a centrist blueprint for the Democratic Party to counter federal "chaos and corruption."

## The "Pennsylvania Model": Operational Efficiency & Economic Growth
*   **"GSD" (Get Shit Done) Philosophy:** Shapiro emphasizes a results-oriented approach to government, focusing on making the bureaucracy move "at the speed of business."
*   **Permitting Reform:** 
    *   **Money-Back Guarantee:** Pennsylvania now offers a guarantee on permits; if the state misses a deadline, the fee is refunded. Out of 40 million permits issued, only five refunds have been required.
    *   **Speed Improvements:** The state has moved from bottom-five to top-five nationally in permitting speed. Professional licenses (e.g., barbers) that previously took 20 days are now issued same-day.
*   **Tax Policy:** Shapiro has cut taxes seven times during his tenure to increase competitiveness. He explicitly opposes wealth taxes or the seizure of unrealized capital gains, arguing that a pro-growth environment is more effective for long-term revenue.
*   **Workforce Development:** 
    *   **Removing Degree Barriers:** Shapiro signed an executive order removing college degree requirements for 60% of state government jobs, focusing on skills and "Generation Tool-Belt" trades.
    *   **Trade Investment:** Tripled funding for vocational-technical (Vo-Tech) and apprenticeship programs.

## Accountability and Anti-Fraud Initiatives
*   **Prosecuting Fraud:** Drawing on his background as Attorney General, Shapiro maintains a zero-tolerance policy for the theft of taxpayer dollars. 
    *   **Medicaid Fraud:** Pennsylvania ranks at the top of the country for Medicaid fraud prosecutions and recoveries.
    *   **COVID Relief:** Aggressive prosecution of PPP loan fraud to ensure funds reach intended recipients.
*   **Public Safety:** 
    *   **Staffing:** Hired 2,000 additional police officers.
    *   **Results:** Reported a 12% drop in violent crime and a 42% reduction in fatal gun violence across the Commonwealth.

## The Future of the Democratic Party & 2028
*   **2024 Election & VP Selection:** Shapiro dismissed claims that he was passed over for the Vice Presidential nomination due to his faith, stating he withdrew from consideration 48 hours before the announcement to focus on governing Pennsylvania.
*   **Democratic "Big Tent":** While acknowledging a "Socialist" wing of the party, Shapiro advocates for a "big tent" where disagreement is healthy but common ground is the priority for governing.
*   **Strategy for 2028:** He argues the party must provide a "calm, competent" alternative to the "chaos, cruelty, and corruption" he attributes to Donald Trump.
*   **Critique of Congress:** Shapiro describes current Congressional leadership (specifically Speaker Johnson) as "pathetic" for acting as a "rubber stamp" for the executive branch rather than a constitutional check.

## Geopolitics: Israel, Iran, and Antisemitism
*   **Antisemitism vs. Policy:** Shapiro insists on separating the condemnation of antisemitism from the critique of Middle East policy. He argues antisemitism must be "universally condemned" without nuance, while Middle East policy requires deep nuance.
*   **Netanyahu Critique:** He characterizes Prime Minister Netanyahu as a leader who has isolated Israel and "fractured" bipartisan American support through dangerous, extremist-aligned policies.
*   **War with Iran:** Shapiro labels the escalating conflict with Iran a "war of choice" by the Trump administration, criticizing the lack of a defined mission or exit strategy. He argues that American interests are poorly served when the U.S. is "led around" by other nations.

## Notable Quotes

> "The way we start the conversation is by recognizing permits are critically important to economic development... if I can give you as a CEO predictability to know your business is going to be opening in six months instead of three years, you’re going to want to invest here." — **Gov. Josh Shapiro**

> "I think the Congress of the United States, the leadership there... they are frankly kind of sad, pathetic people. They have given away their power to folks who are corrupt and to folks who are not acting in an honorable way." — **Gov. Josh Shapiro**

> "On the issue of antisemitism, we have got to be in a place where we universally condemn it... On the issue of Israel and the Middle East... there’s a lot of nuance there. You can be super critical of Israel and you could love your Jewish neighbors and friends." — **Gov. Josh Shapiro**

briefings.title: Market Relief After US-Iran Ceasefire Before Trump Deadline | The Opening Trade 4/8/2026
briefings.tldr: Markets experienced a massive relief rally after the US and Iran agreed to a surprise two-week ceasefire just 90 minutes before a Trump-imposed deadline, sending Brent crude tumbling 14% and European equities surging over 5%.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR:** Markets experienced a massive relief rally after the US and Iran agreed to a surprise two-week ceasefire just 90 minutes before a Trump-imposed deadline, sending Brent crude tumbling 14% and European equities surging over 5%. While the immediate risk of escalation has subsided, significant uncertainty remains regarding the "maximalist" demands of both nations and the logistical complexities of reopening the Strait of Hormuz to over 800 trapped vessels.

## Market Reaction and Volatility
* **Crude Oil Plunge:** Brent crude dropped more than 14% at the open, falling below the $100/barrel mark for the first time in weeks as the immediate threat to Iranian infrastructure evaporated.
* **Equity Surge:** The Euro Stoxx 50 rose 5.3%, while the DAX gained over 5.2% due to its high sensitivity to energy costs.
    * **Sector Winners:** Technology and Luxury saw sharp rebounds; ASML rose 7.6%, while Travel & Leisure gained 7.4% on hopes of lower fuel costs.
    * **Sector Losers:** Energy was the only sector in negative territory, with Shell down 7% and BP down 8% following the oil price collapse.
* **Bond Market Relief:** European bond yields saw "staggering" moves. Italian 10-year BTP yields dropped 34 basis points, and German Bunds fell 18 basis points as markets priced out aggressive rate hikes from the ECB.
* **Hedge Fund Fallout:** Recent volatility has severely impacted leveraged macro funds. Jupiter’s fund lost 12% in March, and Brevan Howard’s master fund fell 6.6%, its worst monthly loss in over 20 years.

## Geopolitical Standoff and the Strait of Hormuz
* **The Ceasefire Agreement:** Mediated by Pakistan with reported influence from China and US Vice President JD Vance, the deal provides a 14-day window for further negotiations in Islamabad.
* **Logistical Bottlenecks:** Approximately 800 vessels remain trapped in the Persian Gulf.
    * **Coordination Challenges:** Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that passage through the Strait would require "coordination with Iran’s armed forces," suggesting Tehran may still exert sovereignty and potentially impose tolls.
    * **Throughput:** While the Strait can handle 100+ ships a day, analysts estimate it will take at least a week to clear the current backlog, assuming no technical or insurance-related delays.
* **Sustained Demands:** Iran is maintaining "maximalist" demands, including the removal of US bases from the region and war reparations. Meanwhile, Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu clarified that the ceasefire with Iran does not necessarily apply to operations against Hezbollah in Lebanon.

## Long-term Macro and Central Bank Outlook
* **Inflation Narrative:** Joachim Klement of Panmure Liberum suggests that "three is the new two" for long-term inflation. While the energy shock may be transitory, deglobalization and defense spending will keep structural inflation higher.
* **Federal Reserve Stance:** New York Fed President John Williams indicated that monetary policy is currently "well-positioned" and favors a wait-and-see approach. He lowered his 2026 growth forecast to 2–2.5% but noted the labor market remains stable at 4.3% unemployment.
* **Real Assets:** Evy Hambro of BlackRock noted that gold and copper remain attractive as "geopolitical insurance." He argued that even if peace holds, governments will continue to spend heavily on defense and energy independence, providing a floor for commodity prices.

## Corporate and Industry Highlights
* **Apple (AAPL):** Bloomberg reports that Apple is on track to launch its first foldable phone in September 2026, alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max models.
* **Private Credit:** Moody’s cut the outlook for Blue Owl Capital’s flagship fund to negative, citing significantly higher redemption requests as investors grow concerned over lax lending standards.
* **Aviation:** IATA Director General Willie Walsh welcomed the ceasefire but warned that jet fuel and ticket prices would likely remain elevated due to the lingering "risk premium" and infrastructure damage in the Middle East.

> "I like to say 'three is the new two' when it comes to long-term inflation rates. The reasons are manifold... higher risk premiums around energy, demographic trends, and the falling away of the disinflationary impact of globalization." 
> — **Joachim Klement**, Head of Strategy at Panmure Liberum

> "The conflict is paused... this is a war that nobody was winning. But I still remain cautious because Iran’s demands are really quite extreme and it’s hard to see them coming out having achieved everything." 
> — **Sanam Vakil**, Director of Middle East and North Africa Program at Chatham House

> "To my mind, monetary policy today is really well-positioned... exactly where it needs to be. We can respond if the situation changes, but right now we can wait and see." 
> — **John Williams**, President of the New York Federal Reserve

briefings.title: Prada Group CEO: Why Patience Beats Trends | Podcast | In Good Company
briefings.tldr: Prada Group CEO Andrea Guerra argues that the luxury industry must return to its "old normal" of exclusivity and patient brand-building, prioritizing emotional storytelling and creative tension over chasing short-term trends.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Prada Group CEO Andrea Guerra argues that the luxury industry must return to its "old normal" of exclusivity and patient brand-building, prioritizing emotional storytelling and creative tension over chasing short-term trends. By leveraging data-driven CRM and revitalizing iconic brands like Miu Miu and Versace, the group aims to scale to a €10 billion ambition while maintaining a founder-led, "rebellious" cultural identity.

## The Return to "Old Normal" in Luxury
* **Normalization of Growth:** Following decades of unsustainable expansion, Guerra believes the industry is entering a period of "normalization" where success depends on returning to exclusivity, value, and selectivity.
* **Exclusivity over Expansion:** 
    * **Store Strategy:** Despite significant growth, Prada has only expanded from 170 to 176 stores in three years. Guerra prefers enlarging existing locations over opening new ones to maintain scarcity.
    * **Hospitality-Driven Retail:** The group is shifting retail spaces toward experience-based models, such as converting entire floors in Hong Kong into "apartments" for exclusive guest use.
* **The "Price" Fallacy:** In true luxury, the goal is to sell an emotion or a dream so effectively that the consumer doesn't question the price. If price becomes the main topic of conversation, the brand has failed its storytelling mission.

## Brand DNA and Creative Tension
* **Prada as Culture:** Prada is defined as a "point of view" rooted in art, architecture, and literature. Guerra maintains that while the world and trends change, the brand's core opinion must remain constant.
* **Miu Miu’s Growth:** 
    * **Inclusive Rebellion:** Miu Miu is described as "rebellious" and "out of the fashion logic," yet inclusive across age groups (25–50). 
    * **Market Potential:** While focused on women’s wear, Guerra sees significant room for growth compared to larger single-gender peers.
* **Creative Management:** Winning brands require a "constant positive tension" between brand management and creative direction. Guerra emphasizes long-term commitments to creative directors over short-term, cyclical hires.

## Strategic Acquisitions and Global Outlook
* **The Versace Turnaround:** 
    * **The Rationale:** Prada Group acquired Versace to bring the iconic Italian brand back to domestic ownership and leverage its roots in "glamour" and "pop" culture. 
    * **Long-Term Nurturing:** Guerra acknowledges past mismanagement and intends to "plant seeds" and "nurture" the brand without expecting immediate, overnight success.
* **Scale and Protection:** The group aims for a €10 billion revenue target, not to become a conglomerate like LVMH, but because scale provides protection in a volatile global market.
* **Regional Dynamics:** 
    * **Europe:** Currently acting as a "tourist market" under pressure, with Asian tourism at 50% of 2019 levels and American tourism declining due to geopolitical concerns.
    * **China:** Following a period of "digestion," the Chinese market is showing a new, slightly positive plateau.

## Technology, Sustainability, and the Young Consumer
* **AI and Personalization:** Prada’s primary use of Artificial Intelligence is within CRM (Customer Relationship Management) to match specific "drops" and messages to individual consumer data, significantly increasing conversion rates.
* **Sustainability as a Standard:** For younger generations, sustainability is a non-negotiable baseline. 
    * **Re-Nylon:** Prada’s transition to sustainable fibers is tied directly to ocean pollution education and specific price points designed to attract younger demographics.
* **Quiet Luxury:** Guerra dismisses the trend of "quiet luxury," stating that the only metric that matters is brand "credibility" over time.

## Leadership and Corporate Evolution
* **Resonant Leadership:** Guerra defines his style as "convincing the mind and heart" that the team is on a shared journey, allowing individuals to express themselves fully.
* **The Power of Debate:** Corporate decisions at Prada are reached through intense, often multi-day debates. Guerra calls this "upper compromise"—reaching the best decision rather than a middle-ground settlement.
* **Operational Efficiency:** 
    * **Energy vs. Experience:** Guerra believes "energy beats experience," though he uses his 25 years as a CEO to listen for what people *aren't* saying.
    * **Anti-Bureaucracy:** He has strictly limited budget presentations to 10 pages to eliminate "formal slide management."

> "Luxury is exclusivity, is selectivity, is value, is dreams, is experience, is hospitality. This is what we have to do. And this is what it has always been." — **Andrea Guerra**

> "It's risky to follow the trends. That's risky. You need to always in your brand... surprise you, comfort you, and we need to do something new together." — **Andrea Guerra**

> "I still think that energy beats experience. And I want to prove it every day... if you don't have experience you cannot hold that position—I don't believe it." — **Andrea Guerra**

briefings.title: The Era of AI Agents | Aaron Levie on The a16z Show
briefings.tldr: As AI agents increasingly outnumber human users, enterprise software must pivot from GUI-first to API/CLI-first architectures, though this transition faces significant hurdles in security, "system of record" stability, and a massive underestimation of future compute economics.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR:** As AI agents increasingly outnumber human users, enterprise software must pivot from GUI-first to API/CLI-first architectures, though this transition faces significant hurdles in security, "system of record" stability, and a massive underestimation of future compute economics.

## The Shift to Agent-First Software Architecture
- **Scale of Usage:** Aaron Levie (CEO, Box) posits a future with 100 to 1,000 times more agents than human users, necessitating a move toward software built primarily for agent interaction via APIs, CLIs, or Model Context Protocol (MCP).
- **Interface Evolution:** While humans struggle with "algorithmic thinking" and creating flowcharts, agents excel at navigating complex software surfaces.
    - **Computer Use vs. Code:** Levie notes a shift from agents purely generating code to "computer use," where agents interact with SaaS tools like humans do, but at massive scale.
    - **The "Mezzanine Step":** Current AI is becoming a consumption layer, mapping natural language to existing software capabilities that humans previously found too complex to use (e.g., advanced Excel or SAP functions).
- **Abstraction Layers:** Steven Sinofsky (Former Microsoft President) argues that "the job moves up a rung." Just as spreadsheets didn't eliminate bankers but changed their skill sets, agents will handle lower-level execution while humans move to higher-level system coordination.

## Security, Liability, and the "System of Record"
- **Agent Identity vs. Human Employees:** Levie argues agents cannot yet be treated like human employees because they lack privacy rights and are highly susceptible to prompt injection.
    - **Liability:** A human employee is accountable for their own mistakes; an agent’s actions are a direct liability for the user who deployed it. 
    - **Security Paradox:** If an agent has access to sensitive data (like M&A documents), it can be social-engineered far more easily than a human, creating a massive risk for enterprises.
- **Integration on the Fly:** There is a fundamental tension between the desire for "on-demand integration" and the need for stability.
    - **CFO/CIO Pushback:** Sinofsky notes that enterprise leaders fear "agents running wild" and breaking systems of record by creating unauthorized or poorly constructed integrations between legacy systems (e.g., SAP and Workday).
    - **The Diffusion Gap:** Startups will move faster because they have "nothing to blow up," while large enterprises like JP Morgan will remain in a "read-only" phase for years to manage risk.

## The Economic Miscalculation of AI
- **Wall Street’s Linear Error:** Sinofsky argues that Wall Street is off by an "order of magnitude" because they view the AI market as a fixed revenue pie. 
    - **Historical Precedent:** Just as the PC and Cloud were initially viewed as finite replacements for existing MIPS or servers, AI will likely result in an asymptotic explosion of resource consumption and new business models.
- **The Engineering Token Budget:** A looming conflict for engineering leaders is determining what percentage of R&D should go toward tokens vs. human salaries.
    - **Usage-Based Pricing:** The high COGS (cost of goods sold) of tokens is forcing the industry toward usage-based models, a shift as significant as the move from perpetual licenses to SaaS.
- **Token Rationing:** Levie predicts a short-term "rationing" phase where companies must decide which employees or experiments get priority access to compute until data center capacity catches up.

## The Future of the Enterprise IT Stack
- **Standardization vs. Meritocracy:** Agents are "smart" at choosing tools based on performance and semantics rather than marketing. This may force software vendors to build better systems rather than just better sales stories.
- **System Fragmentation:** Sinofsky warns that agents might inadvertently fragment IT systems by spinning up de facto "new systems of record" in middleware, leading to security vulnerabilities similar to the "shadow IT" era of the early web.
- **The "Transistor Moment":** While current token costs are high, Sinofsky expects a "transistor moment"—an algorithmic or hardware breakthrough that will eventually make the current obsession with token budgeting irrelevant.

***

**Notable Quotes**

> "If you have a hundred or a thousand times more agents than people, then your software has to be built for agents... we spend as much time now thinking about the agent interface to our tool as we do the human interface." — **Aaron Levie**

> "It's just absurd to think you're going to vibe-code your way to SAP. All of that domain knowledge is not just represented in some well-orchestrated data layer." — **Steven Sinofsky**

> "Wall Street's economics are off by an order of magnitude on how big the opportunity is... they have this fixed revenue pie, but the amount of software being written is going asymptotic." — **Steven Sinofsky**

> "The enterprise customers are going to get left behind by these advanced individuals, which will then start to look like the startups. The startups will move much faster because they have no assets to blow up." — **Aaron Levie**

briefings.title: The Mag Seven Is Cracking: Winners, Losers & What Comes Next
briefings.tldr: The "Magnificent Seven" trade is bifurcating as investors shift focus from pure infrastructure builds to the actual utility and ROI of AI, leaving laggards like Microsoft and Apple under pressure to deliver "Google-level" breakthroughs to justify their valuations.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
The "Magnificent Seven" trade is bifurcating as investors shift focus from pure infrastructure builds to the actual utility and ROI of AI, leaving laggards like Microsoft and Apple under pressure to deliver "Google-level" breakthroughs to justify their valuations.

## AI Infrastructure: The Hyperscaler CAPEX Reality
* **Anthropic’s Massive Scale:** Anthropic’s revenue run rate has surged from $9 billion to $30 billion in a matter of months, validating the massive demand for compute capacity. 
* **Broadcom & Google Synergy:** The partnership between Broadcom and Google on Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) is a major differentiator for Google Cloud (GCP), allowing them to offer specialized hardware that challenges Nvidia’s dominance.
* **The CAPEX Cliff:** While hyperscalers (Amazon, Google, Meta, Microsoft) saw 60% CAPEX growth recently, projections for 2027 suggest a slowdown to ~20%. 
    * **Market Psychology:** Investors are growing wary of whether these companies can maintain a 35-40% growth rate if their primary customers (the big four) slow their infrastructure spending.
* **Nvidia Sentiment:** Despite stellar earnings and 70% expected EPS growth, Nvidia's stock has shown recent weakness. Deepwater has reduced its position by half, citing a "psychological shift" regarding how long hyperscalers can sustain record-breaking spend.

## The Utility Gap: Microsoft and Apple’s "Identity Crisis"
* **Microsoft’s Copilot Struggles:** Sentiment on Microsoft is turning negative as early AI enthusiasm meets reality.
    * **Low Utility:** Gene Munster notes that Copilot has yet to become a "must-use" tool for most professionals, describing current iterations as disappointing in Excel and PowerPoint.
    * **The "Google Moment":** Microsoft needs a definitive AI breakthrough similar to Google’s recent model successes to regain momentum.
* **Apple’s Personalized AI:** Apple is pivoting toward "Personalized AI" with Siri as the focal point, emphasizing data privacy. 
    * **Supercycle Potential:** A hardware device that runs advanced AI locally (safely) could trigger a massive upgrade cycle for "normies" who find current AI tools too complex.
    * **Geopolitical Risk:** Apple remains the most vulnerable megacap to US-China tensions and potential conflict in Taiwan.

## The Future of the Elon Musk Ecosystem
* **SpaceX IPO Dynamics:** SpaceX has filed confidentially for an IPO with a potential $2 trillion valuation. 
    * **Retail Access:** Musk intends to reserve ~30% of the IPO for retail investors, potentially including Tesla shareholders, to maintain his "retail-friendly" brand.
    * **Efficiency:** While SpaceX doesn't *need* public money (given its ability to raise billions privately), being public provides a cheaper, more efficient vehicle for Musk’s long-term Mars vision.
* **Tesla vs. SpaceX:** Tesla has traded poorly since the SpaceX filing, leading to fears of "investor cannibalization."
    * **The Merger Theory:** There is growing speculation that Tesla and SpaceX could eventually merge, combining Tesla’s robotics/AI with SpaceX’s launch capabilities into a single "Master Plan" entity.

## The Changing Workforce and "Intelligent Alpha"
* **Knowledge Work Reductions:** A trend is emerging where companies announce AI investments while simultaneously cutting staff by ~15% (e.g., Pinterest, Morgan Stanley, Oracle).
* **The Practitioner Shift:** Asset managers must evolve from merely *using* AI tools to becoming practitioners who optimize them.
* **Token Pricing Paradox:** While the *cost* of tokens is dropping 10x per year, the total *spend* for companies seeking the "most advanced" intelligence is actually increasing as they chase high-end performance.

***

**Notable Quotes**

> "We are still in the second inning [of AI]... It doesn't happen going from $9 to $30 billion [revenue] over a four-month period unless something bigger is going on." — **Gene Munster**

> "Microsoft needs to have a 'Google moment'... they’re really plagued by two headwinds: seat growth uncertainty for knowledge workers, and the fact that they haven't done something truly exciting in AI yet." — **Gene Munster**

> "If you're in the camp that AI is just going to have an 'impact,' you should probably continue to own these stocks. But for the valuations to hold, it has to have a massive impact." — **Dan Nathan**

> "I have a belief that I might be out of a job in two years... we have to face the reality that machines could take our job." — **Gene Munster**

briefings.title: What 100 Years of American Finance Tells Us About Today
briefings.tldr: The American financial system has transitioned into a "Factory Model" where the industrialization of fundraising and fee-related earnings (FRE) has led to deteriorating underwriting standards and dangerous asset-liability mismatches, particularly within the retail wealth channel.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
The American financial system has transitioned into a "Factory Model" where the industrialization of fundraising and fee-related earnings (FRE) has led to deteriorating underwriting standards and dangerous asset-liability mismatches, particularly within the retail wealth channel.

## The Evolution of the U.S. Financial System
Alan Waxman categorizes the last century of American finance into three distinct systems:

*   **System One (1933–1999):** Defined by the **Glass-Steagall Act** and the separation of commercial banking (deposits) from investment banking (risk-taking).
    *   **Outcome:** Provided 50 years of stability but was not optimized for global competition or maximum economic growth.
*   **System Two (1999–2008):** Triggered by the repeal of Glass-Steagall and deregulation.
    *   **Outcome:** Led to massive leverage (20x–30x) and asset-liability mismatches as investment banks competed with integrated European powerhouses, ultimately culminating in the Global Financial Crisis (GFC).
*   **System Three (2010–Present):** Born from **Basel III** and **Dodd-Frank**, restricting bank leverage and shifting risk-taking to private capital.
    *   **The "Goldilocks" Ideal:** Commercial banks serve as safe, government-backstopped pillars, while private capital (pension funds, endowments) provides risk capital with matched assets and liabilities.
    *   **Current Risk:** This system is under pressure due to behavioral changes that began in 2018.

## The "Factory Model" of Investing
Waxman warns against the industrialization of investment firms, which he calls the "Factory Model." This model prioritizes growth in assets under management (AUM) over artisanal investment returns.

*   **Liability-Driven Strategy:** The process starts with the industrialization of fundraising. Once a firm raises massive amounts of capital, it is forced to industrialize the asset side to deploy that capital quickly.
*   **The Incentive (FRE Multiples):** Markets began valuing **Fee-Related Earnings (FRE)** at 25x–30x multiples. This incentivizes CEOs to raise as much capital as possible to boost the firm's equity value, often at the expense of "carry" (performance-based earnings).
*   **Deteriorating Underwriting:** To maintain high deployment speeds, firms lower their standards, accepting "capped upside" (e.g., 10% returns) while allowing borrowers to strip away collateral or increase leverage.
*   **Narrow Apertures:** The model favors "simple" or "narrow" strategies (e.g., *only* direct lending) because they are easier to sell to the wealth channel, even if the market opportunity in that specific niche has soured.

## The Wealth Channel and Liquidity Myths
The surge of private capital into the retail wealth channel has introduced systemic vulnerabilities similar to those seen in previous financial crises.

*   **The "Semi-Liquid" Fallacy:** Waxman asserts there is no such thing as "semi-liquid." You either have liquid assets or illiquid assets. Giving retail investors quarterly redemption rights on illiquid private loans creates a fundamental asset-liability mismatch.
*   **Pro-cyclical Behavior:** Retail and "mass affluent" investors are notoriously pro-cyclical—they provide capital when things are good and demand it back the moment volatility hits.
*   **Stuck Assets:** Many assets purchased in 2021 and early 2022 are now "stuck." If redemptions exceed limits (typically 5%), it creates the "noise" and stock price volatility currently seen in public private-equity firms.

## Personal Productivity: The "Brain" Sheet
Waxman shares his personal system for maximizing **Return on Time (ROT)** and maintaining "Clarity of Purpose."

*   **The One-Page System:** Waxman organizes his life on a single sheet of paper divided into "Left Brain" (tactical) and "Right Brain" (creative) sections.
    *   **Left Brain:** Contains his top five strategic priorities, high-priority people to call, and health goals (e.g., vitamin D, hip mobility). He rewrites this by hand weekly to "connect dots."
    *   **Right Brain:** A 25-year archive of creative ideas, themes, and business-building thoughts.
*   **Personal Business Plans:** Every employee at Sixth Street is required to write a personal business plan. Waxman argues that people spend weeks evaluating companies but zero time evaluating their own "business plan" for the year.
*   **Career Stages:**
    *   **20s:** Pure education and asking "dumb questions."
    *   **30s:** Ambition and proving oneself, though still making "rookie" mistakes.
    *   **40s:** "Prime Time"—the decade where experience, mistakes, and energy align.
    *   **50s:** Transitioning to mentorship and teaching.

## Creative Destruction and "Facing the Tiger"
*   **AI as a Universal Disrupter:** Waxman views AI as a tool for every industry, not just software. Companies that fail to adopt "agentic capabilities" to drive margins will be left behind.
*   **Facing the Tiger:** Sixth Street’s core ethos. It means running *toward* problems rather than away from them. When a mistake happens or a market shifts, the firm’s culture is to look at the issue head-on without pointing fingers.
*   **The Multi-Strategy Advantage:** Waxman argues that in a world of rapid change, having a "wide aperture" is essential. Narrow investment strategies are "crazy" because they cannot adapt when supply-demand dynamics shift.

> "There is no such thing as semi-liquid. Anyone that’s an investor that’s been through a bunch of cycles—there’s liquid and then there’s illiquid." — **Alan Waxman**

> "The Factory Model... starts on the liability side where you raise all the money, then you have it, then the behavioral change starts. The industrialization of the asset side follows." — **Alan Waxman**

> "We look at the problems head-on, we look at them together and we don't run from them, we run to them. We run right at them. And that’s what 'face the tiger' is." — **Alan Waxman**

briefings.title: White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt holds a briefing with reporters — 4/8/2026
briefings.tldr: President Trump has declared a two-week ceasefire following the 38-day "Operation Epic Fury," which the White House claims successfully dismantled Iran’s military infrastructure and senior leadership.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
President Trump has declared a two-week ceasefire following the 38-day "Operation Epic Fury," which the White House claims successfully dismantled Iran’s military infrastructure and senior leadership. High-level negotiations led by Vice President JD Vance will begin this weekend in Islamabad to seek a long-term diplomatic solution.

## Military Outcomes of Operation Epic Fury
*   **Operational Success:** Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt reported that the 38-day operation exceeded its core objectives, destroying Iran’s defense industrial base and its ability to manufacture or distribute weapons to regional proxies.
*   **Target Statistics:** The U.S. military struck more than 13,000 targets across Iran.
    *   **Ballistic Missiles & Drones:** 450 strikes on ballistic missile units and 800 strikes on drone launching and storage facilities.
    *   **Naval Annihilation:** Over 150 naval vessels were destroyed; Iran now possesses zero operational submarines and has lost 97% of its naval mine inventory.
    *   **Air Dominance:** The Iranian Air Force is "operationally irrelevant," with daily flights dropping from 100 per day to zero.
*   **Leadership Casualties:** U.S. strikes targeted command and control structures over 2,000 times, resulting in the death of senior leaders, including Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.
*   **U.S. Casualties:** The White House confirmed and honored 13 American service members killed during the operation.

## Ceasefire Terms and the "Islamabad Talks"
*   **Negotiation Framework:** After discarding an initial "unserious" 10-point plan from Iran, the Trump administration accepted a modified proposal as a "workable basis" for a 15-point U.S. agreement.
*   **U.S. Negotiating Team:** President Trump is dispatching Vice President JD Vance, Special Envoy Steve Witkoff, and Jared Kushner to Islamabad, Pakistan, for in-person talks starting Saturday.
*   **The "Red Line":** Leavitt emphasized that the total end of Iranian uranium enrichment remains a non-negotiable requirement for any permanent deal.
*   **Strait of Hormuz:** A primary condition of the ceasefire is the "free, safe, and immediate" reopening of the Strait. 
    *   **Tolling Proposals:** The President has floated the idea of a joint U.S.-Iranian venture to charge tolls for passage, though the immediate priority is unrestricted access.
    *   **Conflicting Reports:** While Iranian state media claimed the Strait remained closed, the White House reported an uptick in traffic and expects Iran to honor its private commitment to reopen it.

## Regional and International Relations
*   **Israel and Lebanon:** Prime Minister Netanyahu has expressed support for the ceasefire. However, the administration clarified that Lebanon is **not** included in this specific truce, despite ongoing Israeli strikes in the country.
*   **NATO Criticism:** Leavitt delivered a harsh critique of NATO allies, stating they "failed" by not supporting the U.S. during the 38-day conflict. President Trump is scheduled to meet with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte to discuss the future of the alliance.
*   **China’s Role:** The administration acknowledged high-level coordination with President Xi Jinping’s government in facilitating the ceasefire; President Trump plans to visit China in the coming weeks.
*   **Future Targets:** The White House signaled that the Cuban regime may be the next focus of "maximum pressure" diplomatic or economic efforts, describing the government in Havana as being in a "very weak position."

## Domestic Policy and Legislation
*   **The "Take It Down" Act:** The White House announced the first conviction under this landmark legislation, credited to First Lady Melania Trump. The act targets non-consensual AI-generated explicit images and cyberstalking.
*   **Senior Tax Relief:** Leavitt highlighted the "Working Families Tax Cut," claiming it has eliminated Social Security taxes for nearly 90% of American seniors.
*   **Iranian Deportations:** The administration confirmed the ongoing deportation of relatives of Iranian officials (including the niece of the late General Soleimani) found to be in the U.S. on "fraudulent" asylum or visa claims.

***

**Notable Quotes**

> "The Iranians originally put forward a 10-point plan that was fundamentally unserious, unacceptable, and completely discarded. It was literally thrown in the garbage by President Trump and his negotiating team." — **Karoline Leavitt**

> "Iran's ability to build and stockpile ballistic missiles and long-range drones has also been set back by years compared to where it was six weeks ago... the Iranian Navy was completely annihilated." — **Karoline Leavitt**

> "It’s quite sad that NATO turned their backs on the American people over the course of the last six weeks when it’s the American people who have been de-funding their defense." — **Karoline Leavitt**

> "The President’s red lines, namely the end of Iranian enrichment in Iran, have not changed. And the idea that President Trump would ever accept an Iranian wishlist as a deal is completely absurd." — **Karoline Leavitt**
